title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
abstract: arXiv:2611.22639v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. This study introduces a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking CPG model embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop. A composite synchronization metric is developed, integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. Its performance is evaluated across systematically varied stimulation waveforms and synaptic configurations. Statistical analysis reveals that stimulation type dominates regime determination, with tonic drive yielding the most robust antiphase synchronization. translated_title: 面向运动控制的仿生脉冲神经网络架构中反相同步的分层控制
translated_abstract: 中枢模式发生器（CPG）为自适应运动控制提供了生物启发的基础，然而在脉冲神经网络中系统地表征其动态模式仍然具有挑战性。本研究提出了一个框架，用于识别和稳定嵌入闭环神经肌肉回路中的仿生脉冲CPG模型的反相同步。研究开发了一种复合同步度量指标，综合了相位相干性、幅度平衡和时间稳定性三个维度，并在系统变化的刺激波形和突触配置下评估其性能。统计分析表明，刺激类型主导着动态模式的确定，其中持续型驱动产生了最稳健的反相同步；周期性输入则会诱发非线性饱和和依赖上下文的网络路由。尽管突触权重本身仅表现出有限的判别能力，但它们显著调节了同步的稳健性。
tldr: 该研究提出了一个在闭环神经肌肉回路中识别并稳定仿生脉冲中枢模式发生器反相同步的分层控制框架，通过融合相位相干性、幅度平衡与时间稳定性的复合度量，发现刺激类型（尤其是持续型驱动）是决定同步模式的主导因素。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a hierarchical control framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking CPG model embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop, using a composite synchronization metric to reveal that stimulation type—particularly tonic drive—dominates the robustness of synchronization regimes.
